name: Learn: Update Existing Deployments in place (hardened)
objective: CKAD › Application Deployment. Drill EVERY way to change a Deployment that already exists — WITHOUT deleting it: scale, rolling image update, rollback, set resources, inject config, change strategy, targeted JSON patch, and rollout restart. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Four pre-seeded running Deployments in 'deploy-learn'. You never delete and rebuild — you modify in place with scale / set / patch / edit / rollout. Each Check shows which requirements you met and why any failed.

questions.title: Scale in place
questions.teach:
Scaling changes only `.spec.replicas` — it does **not** touch the pod template, so no rollout happens. Never delete+recreate just to change replica count.

- `kubectl scale deployment/<name> --replicas=N` — the fast path.
- `kubectl scale deployment/<name> --current-replicas=2 --replicas=5` — conditional (only if currently 2).
- `kubectl patch deployment <name> -p '{"spec":{"replicas":5}}'` or `kubectl edit` — declarative edits.

**Gotchas:** an **HPA** targeting the Deployment overrides manual `scale` within seconds; `readyReplicas` lagging `replicas` just means pods are still coming up; scaling to 0 parks a workload without deleting it.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `frontend` in `deploy-learn` exists with 2 replicas. Scale it **in place** to **4**.

Target: `frontend` has 4 ready replicas (and you did not delete it).
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn scale deployment/frontend --replicas=4
kubectl -n deploy-learn get deploy frontend

verification.description: frontend scaled to 4 ready replicas (in place)

questions.title: Rolling image update
questions.teach:
Changing the pod template (the image) triggers a **rolling update** — a new ReplicaSet scales up while the old scales down. Do it in place; don't recreate.

- `kubectl set image deployment/<name> <container>=<newimg>` — the targeted way. **Check the container name first** (`kubectl get deploy <name> -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].name}'`) — it isn't always the deployment name.
- `kubectl edit`, `kubectl patch`, or re-`apply` an edited manifest also roll it.
- `kubectl rollout status deployment/<name>` to watch.

**Gotchas:** a rollout only happens if `.spec.template` actually changes; the old ReplicaSet is kept (scaled to 0) for rollback — that history is your undo button.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `api` in `deploy-learn` runs `nginx:1.25` (container named `api`). Perform a rolling update to `nginx:1.26` in place.

Target: the update to `nginx:1.26` is recorded in `api`'s ReplicaSet history (this evidence survives the rollback in the next step).
questions.hint: `kubectl -n deploy-learn set image deployment/api api=nginx:1.26`, then `kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout status deployment/api`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn set image deployment/api api=nginx:1.26
kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout status deployment/api

verification.description: api rolling-updated to nginx:1.26 (recorded in history)

questions.title: Roll back a bad release
questions.teach:
`kubectl rollout undo` reverts the pod template to a previous revision — in place, no delete.

- `kubectl rollout history deployment/<name>` lists revisions; `--revision=N` shows one.
- `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>` → previous revision; `--to-revision=N` → a specific one.

**Gotchas:** an undo is itself a **new revision** (it doesn't delete the bad one); it restores the **whole** pod template of that revision (image, env, resources…), not just the image — so roll back *before* layering on other template edits; you can only reach revisions still kept by `revisionHistoryLimit` (default 10).
questions.prompt:
`nginx:1.26` misbehaves. Roll `api` back so its image returns to `nginx:1.25`.

Target: `api`'s current image is `nginx:1.25` again and the rollout is complete (3/3).
questions.hint: `kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout undo deployment/api`, then `rollout status`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout undo deployment/api
kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout status deployment/api

verification.description: api rolled back to nginx:1.25 (rollout complete)

questions.title: Set resources in place
questions.teach:
`kubectl set resources` edits requests/limits on a live controller's template (triggering a rollout) — no need to hand-edit YAML or recreate.

- `kubectl set resources deployment/<name> --requests=cpu=100m,memory=128Mi --limits=cpu=200m,memory=256Mi`.
- Target a specific container with `-c <name>` when there are several.
- `kubectl edit` / `kubectl patch` do the same declaratively.

**Gotchas:** `requests` drive scheduling, `limits` cap usage (memory over limit → OOMKilled); setting requests == limits for cpu+mem makes the pod **Guaranteed** QoS; units are exact (`100m`, `128Mi`).
questions.prompt:
On Deployment `cache` in `deploy-learn`, set container resources **in place**: requests `cpu=100m, memory=128Mi`; limits `cpu=200m, memory=256Mi`.

Target: `cache`'s container has exactly those requests and limits.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn set resources deployment/cache --requests=cpu=100m,memory=128Mi --limits=cpu=200m,memory=256Mi
kubectl -n deploy-learn get deploy cache -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources}'

questions.title: Inject config from a ConfigMap
questions.teach:
`kubectl set env` injects environment config into a live controller in place.

- `kubectl set env deployment/<name> KEY=val` — one literal.
- `kubectl set env deployment/<name> --from=configmap/<cm>` — adds one env var **per key** of the ConfigMap (each as a `configMapKeyRef`).
- `kubectl set env deployment/<name> --from=secret/<s>` — same for a Secret.
- `kubectl set env deployment/<name> --list` — show current env; `KEY-` removes one.

**Gotchas:** `--from=configmap` wires individual `configMapKeyRef` env vars (vs `envFrom` bulk, which you'd hand-write); env from a ConfigMap is read **once at pod start** — changing the ConfigMap later needs a `rollout restart` (step 8) to take effect.
questions.prompt:
ConfigMap `worker-cfg` (keys `LOG_LEVEL`, `REGION`) exists in `deploy-learn`. Inject **all its keys** as environment variables into the `worker` Deployment, in place, using `kubectl set env --from`.

Target: `worker`'s container has env `LOG_LEVEL` and `REGION`, each sourced from ConfigMap `worker-cfg`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n deploy-learn set env deployment/worker --from=configmap/worker-cfg`, then `kubectl -n deploy-learn set env deployment/worker --list`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn set env deployment/worker --from=configmap/worker-cfg
kubectl -n deploy-learn set env deployment/worker --list

verification.description: worker env LOG_LEVEL + REGION sourced from ConfigMap worker-cfg

questions.title: Change the update strategy
questions.teach:
`.spec.strategy` controls how pods are replaced on a template change — change it in place.

- `RollingUpdate` (default): `maxSurge` / `maxUnavailable` (number or %).
- `Recreate`: kill all old pods, then create new ones (brief downtime, never two versions at once).
- `kubectl patch deployment <name> -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"Recreate","rollingUpdate":null}}}'` or `kubectl edit`.

**Gotchas:** `Recreate` must **not** carry a `rollingUpdate` block — set it `null` or the API rejects it; `maxSurge` and `maxUnavailable` can't both be 0; changing the strategy alone does not trigger a rollout.
questions.prompt:
Change Deployment `cache`'s update strategy to **Recreate**, in place.

Target: `cache`'s `.spec.strategy.type` is `Recreate`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn patch deployment cache -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"Recreate","rollingUpdate":null}}}'
kubectl -n deploy-learn get deploy cache -o jsonpath='{.spec.strategy.type}'

questions.title: Targeted change with a JSON patch
questions.teach:
`kubectl patch` has **three** patch types — know when each applies:
- **strategic** (default for native kinds): merges by schema, so list items merge by key (e.g. containers by name).
- **merge** (`--type=merge`, RFC 7386): replaces whole objects/lists — a JSON merge patch.
- **json** (`--type=json`, RFC 6902): **op-based** (`add`/`replace`/`remove`) targeting an exact **path**, e.g. `/spec/template/spec/containers/0/imagePullPolicy` — the precise scalpel for one field or a list index.

Example: `kubectl patch deploy x --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/imagePullPolicy","value":"IfNotPresent"}]'`.

**Gotchas:** JSON-patch paths are 0-indexed and must exist (use `add` to create); strategic merge can't reorder/replace a list element the way a JSON patch index can; quote the JSON carefully in the shell.
questions.prompt:
Using a **JSON patch** (`kubectl patch --type=json`), set the `imagePullPolicy` of the container in Deployment `frontend` to `IfNotPresent`, in place.

Target: `frontend`'s container `imagePullPolicy` is `IfNotPresent`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n deploy-learn patch deployment frontend --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/imagePullPolicy","value":"IfNotPresent"}]'` (use `add` instead of `replace` if the field isn't set yet).
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn patch deployment frontend --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/imagePullPolicy","value":"IfNotPresent"}]'
kubectl -n deploy-learn get deploy frontend -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].imagePullPolicy}'

verification.description: frontend container imagePullPolicy == IfNotPresent (via JSON patch)

questions.title: Reload config with rollout restart
questions.teach:
`kubectl rollout restart` rolls a Deployment's pods **with no spec change** — the clean way to pick up a changed ConfigMap/Secret (env is read once at pod start, so editing the config alone doesn't update running pods).

- `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name>` — stamps `spec.template.metadata.annotations["kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt"]` with a timestamp, which changes the template and triggers a fresh rollout.
- `kubectl rollout status` to confirm; `kubectl rollout pause`/`resume` batch several edits into one rollout.

**Gotchas:** restart ≠ delete — the controller rolls new pods gracefully; a mounted ConfigMap **volume** updates live (no restart needed), but env/`envFrom` from a ConfigMap does not.
questions.prompt:
Roll the `worker` Deployment's pods in place (no spec change) so they'd pick up a changed ConfigMap — using `rollout restart`.

Target: `worker`'s pod template carries the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` annotation.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout restart deployment/worker`, then `kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout status deployment/worker`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout restart deployment/worker
kubectl -n deploy-learn rollout status deployment/worker

verification.description: worker rolled via rollout restart (restartedAt annotation present)
